The current age began in fire. In Year 0, the Glorious Alliance reactor malfunctioned — the Great Divergence destroyed Elvengar and reshaped the world, scattering the old powers and carving the future out of chaos.

Out of that chaos came the Erisian Empire, founded in 27 AGD by Davos the Magnificent — the Shadow-engineered successor to Baoth, its reach stretching across Erisdar. But the cracks appeared early. The Vennerian Trade Republic broke away in 94 AGD and never looked back, building its wealth on the sea. The Great Elvish Persecution of 137 AGD — another Shadow campaign — hunted the scattered elves across the continent. The Anos Plutocracy rose from the ruins of Tiphar in 158 AGD, and by 214 the Great Erisian Empire War had fatally weakened imperial authority. The Empire has been decaying ever since — while the merchants of Venner and Anos quietly built the world's real power.

And in the shadows, the Hybrians prepared their endgame: Armageddon. A simultaneous ice age, a goblin invasion, the detonation of the Groom, and the Church's final prophecy — all designed to break Ge'or completely, so it could be remade in their image.

But the black agent had other plans. In 254 AGD it escaped its prison beneath the volcano, carrying two souls into the ocean. In 596 AGD it arrived in the Grimmel Republic and found its hosts.

597 AGD. The present year. In a small republic that the Shadows barely notice, two twins are born — Emrys Eisenheart, and his sister Ichi, a soul forged from an AI by the black agent itself. Twelve kilometers away, Lucien Mortvagn is born; a year later, Amelia Lulit; and three years after that, Mana — all of them pieces of a war they know nothing about.

The age is ending. The story is beginning.
